metrics.outcome: Out of budget: 0 of 58 units left, less than the cheapest rate-card part (5), so no new workflow can be funded.
metrics.brief: Brew Lab, Indiranagar, Bengaluru. One-page site with menu, hours, location and pre-order for pickup. We want a big photo gallery of the cafe AND a detailed story section about each of our three coffee farms. Keep costs low.

raises.why: the Requester chose option 2: Raise the budget by 23 and build the phone fix plus the three farm stories. The photo gallery is dropped from this site.

list.outcome: Adaptation accepted Priority's COUNTER: Page shell, hours and location (15), Menu and pickup pre-order form (15) goes to the validator.

open_inputs: Street address and map pin for the cafe
Phone number and/or WhatsApp or email for receiving pre-orders
Pickup time rules (slot length, lead time)
Names, locations and stories of the three coffee farms
Farm photos and key details (altitude, variety, process)

review.verdict: The department built everything the Requester approved (9 of 10 done-when items, with the gallery dropped by choice) with no validator or role refusals, but the run ended out of budget and never reached 'done' because the charter was not updated to record the dropped gallery.

identity.note: Good: one decision-ready question with costed options [20], and it correctly recorded the gallery drop in its reasoning [36]. Weak: its first cost sum was wrong ('38 more, roughly 68' [17], corrected to about 48 more in [20]). Both its Requester-addressed messages were redirected [18], [36]. It declared done while Audit still showed a fail [37], and the final charter still has dropped_from_brief empty, so its 'I am recording' [36] had no visible effect.

adaptation.note: Split the work into small workflows, accepted Priority's counter in 2 attempts [4]-[6], and after the Requester chose, proposed exactly what fit (8+20 of 28) and asked Identity to record the drop [24]. Flaws: [4] calls W1+W2+W3 'within 35' at 40, and it priced the gallery at 10 when it later said 10 to 20 [19], so the 'full scope 60' figure was too low.

priority.note: Clear COUNTER with reasons and trade-off [5], then GRANT with stop-loss [25]. Correctly left the charter change to Identity [25]. Envelope checks were fast and in role. Cost: it granted down to zero reserve, so no retry or rework could be funded [25], [38].

coordination.note: Stated its scheduling rule every turn, respected the same-file dependency order (W-1, W-2, W-3, W-4), passed the Builder's unmeasured-fix note on [30], and never overreached. Little was tested: nothing was ever held.

audit.note: Mechanical check ran both cycles and caught the 78px overflow [15]. It routed the budget and policy items to Identity, not Adaptation, and refused to rewrite work. It raised the dropped-gallery mismatch correctly [35]. Miss: [16] says 8 of 10 pass while its own tally gives 7 (6 PASS + 1 warning); Identity restated it as 7 [17].

builder.note: Four runs, no redirects, stayed in scope, flagged what it did not measure [29], and finished at 23 KB, well under the 60 KB limit. The v2 page it shipped overflowed 78px at 360px, against a mobile-first standard, and cost 8 to fix.

went_well: The brief's built-in conflict (gallery AND farm stories AND low cost) was surfaced early and sent to the Requester as one question with four costed options [20]. Only 1 Requester question was used.
Priority and Adaptation settled the funding disagreement themselves in 2 attempts, with no escalation (conflict C-1).
Zero validator refusals, zero role refusals, zero failed workflows, zero stuck turns.
The code-run phone check found a real defect the agents had not noticed (78px overflow) [15] and confirmed the fix (0px) [34]. Mechanical checks beat agent claims here.
No invented facts: unknown prices, hours, address, contacts and farm details are marked placeholders, and eight open inputs are listed in the charter.
problems: The run ended without 'done'. The Requester dropped the gallery, Audit still failed item 7 [35], Identity's done verdict was rejected [37], and the final charter shows dropped_from_brief as empty. Nothing in the system could clear the failing item.
The 360px overflow shipped in v2 and was only found at Audit [15]. The fix took 8 of the 58 spend (about 14%) and a second cycle.

Costs were understated early. The gallery with lightbox was priced 10 [4] and later 20 [19]. By the rate card, full scope is about 78 (15+15+20+20+8), which is over the 70 cap. The department could not have built the full brief within cap, and nobody said so.
Option 1 in [20] adds 43 to a budget of 35, giving 78, above the 70 cap. Whether code would have allowed it is unverified.

Identity's two Requester-addressed messages were redirected to Adaptation [18], [36], although team.md allows Identity to Requester. [18] cost an extra Adaptation turn before the question was asked. The code seems to allow that route only for pause questions.
Pre-order total and placeholder marking were read from code, not run or rendered [36]. Whether the pre-order works is unverified.
Zero reserve at the end [25] means any Audit defect after the last run cannot be fixed. The budget ran out with 0 of 58.
learnings: Add a code step that applies a Requester-approved drop to the charter (done_when, rules, dropped_from_brief) and re-scores Audit against it. Evidence: [35]-[37] and the empty dropped_from_brief. Without it, any scope-cut run cannot finish.

Run the code phone and desktop check after each build workflow, or at least after the first page shell, not only at Audit. Trade-off: slightly more code time, no model cost. Evidence: the overflow came from W-1/W-2 and cost 8 to fix [15], [29].

Have Priority hold a small reserve (for example the cost of one fix) or require a reserve note on the last grant. Evidence: zero reserve [25] and no recovery path at [38]. Trade-off: one feature may be cut sooner.

Price from the rate card in code, not from agent estimates. All four workflows were charged exactly the agent estimate, so this run says nothing about estimate accuracy. The gallery's 10 versus 20 [4], [19] shows agents drift.
Check Requester options against the budget cap before showing them (Option 1 totals 78 versus cap 70 [20]). If the full brief cannot fit under cap, say so in the first Priority counter.
Align the route check with team.md. Identity to Requester is listed as allowed but was redirected twice [18], [36]. Either document the rule or allow the J2.h goal-reached message.

Test next: same brief with a cap above 78, and a variant where Audit finds a real defect with no budget left. HOLD, REFUSE, Identity conflict rulings and parked workflows were never exercised (held_ever 0, refuses 0, resolved_by_identity 0), so those paths are untested.
Evidence is thin on site quality: I saw the metrics and chat only, not the HTML. Content, pre-order behavior and appearance rest on Audit's code read.

events.detail: C-1: Adaptation vs Priority about what to fund in cycle 1
35 -> 58 (asked +23, cap 70; the Requester chose option 2: Raise the budget by 23 and build the phone fix plus the three farm stories. The photo gallery is dropped from this site.)
Identity declared done, but Audit still has failing items, so done-when can't hold. Rework continues.
